title: Governance of Sustainability and Capstone Workshop
summary: Brings the programme together around board oversight, accountability, remuneration and capability for sustainability, with a workshop in which participants assess their own firm.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Brings the programme together around board oversight, accountability, remuneration and capability for sustainability, with a workshop in which participants assess their own firm.
Learning Objectives: Design governance and accountability for sustainability risks and commitments
Assess the board's capability to oversee sustainability matters
Produce a prioritised action plan for the firm's sustainability approach
Syllabus: Board oversight, committees and management accountability
Seeing the firm the way a supervisor does: a sustainability self-assessment
Workshop: the firm's twelve-month sustainability action plan
Intended Audience: Risk, compliance and sustainability professionals in regulated firms
Portfolio managers, product developers and stewardship teams
Finance, reporting and senior management staff responsible for sustainability disclosures
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of risk, compliance, investment or reporting in a regulated firm is helpful. No specialist sustainability background is required.
Core Reading: ISSB, IFRS S1 General Requirements and IFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures (2023)
TCFD, Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (2017)
IOSCO, Recommendations on Sustainability-Related Practices, Policies, Procedures and Disclosure in Asset Management (2021)
TNFD, Recommendations of the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (2023)
